method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (the text's no where it says no; NOTHING, with a NOTHING-kind tag, where it does not answer); the dates in one module, the rules and exported questions in another, the cases in a third; one regulative rule (commencing within the time the governing place's limitation law allows, made part of the law applied by s 5) run by EVALTRACE inside an exported question that takes only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.

checks.command: l4 run clpa-dates.l4 ; l4 run clpa-claims.l4 ; l4 run clpa-cases.l4
checks.result: 59 assertions written, 59 satisfied, 0 errors, 0 warnings in every file (2026-11-07)
checks.note: l4 run exits 0 even when an assertion fails, so the diagnostics are what was read. Expected values worked by hand from the text.

scope: The whole operative Act, from the claimant's seat. In: s 3 (application, including New Zealand), s 4 (court, limitation law), s 5 (characterization of limitation laws), s 6 (exercise of discretion under limitation law); s 2's commencement date. Out: s 1, s 2 (machinery); the proclamations under s 2 and s 3(2) (not deposited; asked as facts); the limitation laws of the other places (their last day asked as a fact). Reasons in NOTES.md.
